From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" labels

The Seller's package says that clauses marked [STANDARD] were "cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. It says the positions were "settled at principal level," are "FINAL," and that the Buyer has "already accepted" the disclosure and limitation package. These are the Seller's own assertions. Nothing in our records supports them. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its labels. Several items marked [STANDARD] (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident) are described in the letter as unresolved: "NOT included," "NOT been repaid," "preliminary." The "market context" figures are also unsupported advocacy.

**Action:** Before responding, confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether any term was in fact agreed. Our mark-up should state that no term is agreed until the SPA is signed.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher cap, such as 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m), or 20% only if backed by W&I cover and a retention or escrow. The cap must apply to general warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at a higher cap. If 20% is conceded, trade it for W&I and a retention, and keep specific indemnities, fundamental, tax and fraud claims outside the cap. *Reason:* 4.8m is thin given the known risks (a 30% revenue customer, a privacy incident, IP chain-of-title).

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04% of price, so above the "1%" they cite), recoverable only for the excess (a deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 5k–10k. Related claims should aggregate toward the de minimis. A tipping basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k) that, once exceeded, recovers from the first dollar. No basket or de minimis for fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter as above. *Reason:* A 250k deductible plus a 25k per-claim filter would let a large volume of real loss go unrecovered.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months. It also proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, which covers at least one full audited cycle after Completion.
  - Tax: the Commissioner's amendment period plus 60–90 days (practically about 5 years).
  - Fundamental warranties: 6–7 years.
  - Specific indemnities: their own periods.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and strike the catch-all. *Reason:* The default-to-all wording silently imports the 18-month bar into tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, share capital) capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket and a 6–7 year period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* If title fails, the Buyer has paid 24m for nothing, so a 4.8m cap is not a simplification but a 19.2m exposure.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out. None of the limitations, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions should apply to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, the Company's management, or its advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on this, as it is non-negotiable. *Reason:* "Any nature" wording invites argument that fraud and misleading-conduct claims (for example under ACL s 18) are capped or barred, and the non-reliance clause strengthens that argument.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2, 1.4)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records." DL 1.4 adds that nothing admits that any consent or remediation is required.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only. A matter should count as disclosed only if it is fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify its nature and scope. The data room should not be generally disclosed. Public records should be limited to named searches at a fixed date. Specific indemnities should not be qualified by disclosure at all.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. Accept only the specific paragraphs, tested against each warranty. *Reason:* General data-room disclosure would cancel most warranties, including those covering the very defects the letter admits.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-sandbagging clause, where the Buyer's knowledge does not reduce its claims. At minimum, the SPA should be silent. As a fallback, only the actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge individuals of matters fairly disclosed should count. Advisers' knowledge and constructive knowledge should be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Strike cl 8.3 and replace it with a pro-sandbagging clause. *Reason:* Constructive "discoverable" knowledge, combined with general disclosure, makes the warranty package close to worthless.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Per DL 2, there is no consent yet and the clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent requiring unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form the Buyer is satisfied with.
  - Any clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer.
  - Seller to use best endeavours.
  - The condition waivable by the Buyer only, with a long-stop date and a walk right.
  - A specific indemnity, or a price adjustment, if Bluefen terminates or re-prices because of the change of control.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "satisfied on delivery." *Reason:* Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30% of FY26 revenue. A consent with unmet conditions does not protect that revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and not repaid (DL 3).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The facility treated as Debt and repaid at Completion out of the price through the funds flow.
  - A payoff letter before Completion.
  - A deed of release, discharge of all security and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables.
  - Riverlark's waiver of the clause 8.1 change-control default, if repayment is not simultaneous.
- **Recommendation:** Reject release after Completion. *Reason:* This deal is debt-free. Releasing after Completion leaves 3.2m of secured debt, and a possible change-of-control default, in the Company the Buyer now owns.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005, funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. On-costs are unaddressed (DL 5).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation and the employer's share of PAYG/on-costs, defined as Transaction Costs or Debt and deducted from the price.
  - Or the Seller funds them at Completion, paid through Company payroll.
  - A specific indemnity in either case.
- **Recommendation:** Require these amounts to be itemised and deducted. *Reason:* The Company, not the Seller, is the employer and will bear the liability. Leaving it out of the funds flow is a hidden price increase of about 420k plus on-costs.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010). Transfer of Project Materials under DD-004 cl 7.3 is conditional on cleared payment. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Evidence that SOW3 has been paid in full, plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, as a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
  - An indemnity covering all loss from any defect in the Company's title to the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs, and customer losses.
  - The indemnity outside the cap and basket, with a longer survival period.
  - A retention until the assignment is delivered.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the indemnity as "adequate." *Reason:* The real risk is that the Company does not own its product IP, and that risk is far larger than an unpaid 180k invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sched 6, DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" that is not expected to be material. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification status are unknown as at 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Immediate disclosure of the current status. It is now 5 November 2026, so the 30-day assessment window under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme has very likely passed. We need to know whether an assessment was completed, whether OAIC or individuals were notified, and the forensic findings.
  - A specific indemnity, not qualified by disclosure and outside the cap and basket, covering regulatory penalties to the extent the law allows, notification and remediation costs, and customer and third-party claims.
  - A retention or escrow.
  - Covenants on how the incident is managed before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation and require the indemnity plus a status update before signing. *Reason:* Business contact data is still personal information, and a possibly missed notification deadline is a live regulatory exposure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) described as ordinary-course costs. DL 8 does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of all three contracts, with term, termination rights and commitment profile.
  - An explanation of why one arrangement was split into three. Check whether the split avoided an approval or materiality threshold.
  - Any pre-Completion committed or prepaid amounts treated as debt-like, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent to further renewals.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without diligence. *Reason:* Linked contracts just under a threshold are a classic red flag, and their nature is undisclosed.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single limitation regime for "all Claims of any nature." Tax and IP are folded into the general regime. Title is treated like the general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct categories, each with its own cap, threshold and time limit:
  1. General warranties
  2. Fundamental warranties
  3. Tax warranties and tax indemnity
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Bluefen if applicable)
  5. Covenant and leakage breaches
  6. Fraud, which is unlimited
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clauses 12 and 13 on this basis. *Reason:* A single bucket lets the general cap and 18-month bar defeat the protections that matter most.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The share register reconciled against an ASIC company extract.
  - The constitution and share certificates.
  - Confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights to issue shares exist, and no shareholder agreement or pre-emption rights.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Releases of any security over the shares.
  - A fundamental title warranty (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Treat the register as a starting point only, and complete independent verification before signing. *Reason:* A company's internal register is self-generated evidence and does not prove unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for all pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax on the DD-005 bonuses, capped at 100% of price and running for the amendment period plus a margin.
  - Full tax warranties.
  - Enhanced IP warranties (ownership, open-source, no infringement, employee and contractor assignments) with a higher cap and longer period, given this is a SaaS target.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open. *Reason:* These terms have not been negotiated. Folding them into a 20%/18-month regime is the Seller's proposal, not an agreed position.

---

## Other matters to pick up in the mark-up
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm the notification obligation is satisfied before Completion. Obtain a copy of the lease to verify the Seller's reading that landlord consent is not required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Check whether the assignment restriction is drafted widely enough to catch a change of control. Get our own reading of the clause rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- **Overall exposure:** The identified items alone (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m plus on-costs, Sandbar 0.33m, Ironquay, the incident, Bluefen's 3.6m of revenue) show why the Seller's package of general disclosure, buyer knowledge, a single regime and a 20% cap is unacceptable as a whole, not just clause by clause.

I can prepare a responsive issues list or a clause-level mark-up of clauses 8.3, 12 and 13 on this basis.
